headline: Apple's Siri AI finally works, but feels anticlimactic
summary: After years of delays, Apple's revamped Siri is now in beta with iOS 27, understanding context and answering questions, but the AI race has already moved far ahead.
details: Apple's long-awaited AI-powered Siri has arrived in the consumer beta of iOS 27, finally delivering on promises of contextual understanding and broad knowledge access.
The new Siri allows for natural, back-and-forth conversations with adjustable voice pacing and can be interacted with via typing or a dedicated app for the first time.
It can now accurately find personal information like photos, emails, and contacts, even when users are unsure of the specifics, and can even extract data from screenshots.
Users can launch websites and apps, get directions, edit photos, draft emails, and play audiobooks through Siri, with the assistant now consistently playing requested media.
Siri can also brainstorm with users, help refine ideas, suggest recipes based on available ingredients, and provide real-time information like event schedules and band tour dates.
The AI assistant can be used in the camera's viewfinder to identify real-world objects or assist with tasks like splitting restaurant bills.
These advancements are powered by Apple's partnership with Google, utilizing Gemini AI models trained and refined with Apple's proprietary Foundation Models.
Despite its functionality, the arrival of a working Siri feels less revolutionary and more like fixing a long-standing issue, as the AI race has advanced significantly.
The general public will gain access to the new Siri with the official release of iOS 27, expected in September.
caption:
Apple's Siri AI is finally here and it actually works. But after years of delays and the rapid advancement of AI, the launch feels surprisingly anticlimactic.

Apple's long-awaited AI-powered Siri has arrived in the consumer beta of iOS 27, finally delivering on promises of contextual understanding and broad knowledge access.

The new Siri allows for natural, back-and-forth conversations with adjustable voice pacing and can be interacted with via typing or a dedicated app for the first time.

It can now accurately find personal information like photos, emails, and contacts, even when users are unsure of the specifics, and can even extract data from screenshots.

Users can launch websites and apps, get directions, edit photos, draft emails, and play audiobooks through Siri, with the assistant now consistently playing requested media.

Siri can also brainstorm with users, help refine ideas, suggest recipes based on available ingredients, and provide real-time information like event schedules and band tour dates.

The AI assistant can be used in the camera's viewfinder to identify real-world objects or assist with tasks like splitting restaurant bills.

These advancements are powered by Apple's partnership with Google, utilizing Gemini AI models trained and refined with Apple's proprietary Foundation Models.

Despite its functionality, the arrival of a working Siri feels less revolutionary and more like fixing a long-standing issue, as the AI race has advanced significantly.

The general public will gain access to the new Siri with the official release of iOS 27, expected in September.
